journey.title: Type a check-in date, then Tab to the guests field
journey.goal: After typing a date and pressing Tab, focus stays on the next field so the user can keep filling the form

functionalJourney.title: Pick a check-in day with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Clicking a day fills the check-in date and the guests field still takes input

guards.title: Paging months with the pointer keeps keyboard focus in the date field
guards.goal: After clicking Next month, focus is back in the date field so arrow keys and typing keep working

plan.root_cause: The datepicker does not handle the Tab key, so when the picker is open pressing Tab does not close it and focus remains trapped, preventing natural tab navigation to the next form field.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a case for keyCode 9 (Tab) in the _onKeyChange handler to hide the datepicker, allowing the Tab key to move focus to the next focusable element as expected.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Users can navigate away from the datepicker using the Tab key, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard and 2.4.3 Focus Order, allowing seamless form completion.
functional_risks: Hiding the datepicker on Tab could interrupt a user who intends to use Tab for internal navigation, but the datepicker does not use Tab for moving between its internal controls, so risk is low.
verification_requirements: After typing a valid date in the check-in field and pressing Tab, focus must move to the guests input field.
The datepicker widget must be closed (hidden) when Tab is pressed.
Subsequent entry into the guests field should work normally.

plan.root_cause: The datepicker's _onKeyChange handler does not handle the Tab key (keyCode 9). When the datepicker is open, pressing Tab does not close it, and the open datepicker interferes with the browser's default focus movement, leaving focus trapped on the check-in field.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a case for keyCode 9 (Tab) in the _onKeyChange handler to call self.hide(), closing the datepicker and allowing the browser's default Tab navigation to move focus to the next form field.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Users can navigate away from the datepicker using the Tab key, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard and 2.4.3 Focus Order, allowing seamless form completion.
functional_risks: Hiding the datepicker on Tab could interrupt a user who intends to use Tab for internal navigation, but the datepicker does not use Tab for moving between its internal controls, so risk is low.
verification_requirements: After typing a valid date in the check-in field and pressing Tab, focus must move to the guests input field.
The datepicker widget must be closed (hidden) when Tab is pressed.
Subsequent entry into the guests field should work normally.
